mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least three consecutive months, investors anticipate future rate cuts, which lowers the real discount rate and boosts equity present-value pricing, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the next 60 days are not statistically different from the 12-month pre-signal baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or the Fed raises rates within 3 months after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat, and the correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE turns negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests robust industrial demand without price pressures, prompting optimism about corporate earnings and equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 2% month-over-month while CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the next 20 days are negative despite repeated similar INDPRO/CPIAUCSL patterns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months, despite stable or growing GDP demand proxies (GDPC1), suggests the Fed may hold rates steady longer, reducing discount-rate expectations and supporting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for three consecutive months and GDPC1 > 1.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in all similar low-inflation, growing-demand regimes over the past decade.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months triggers a preemptive rate hike by the Fed, which increases the real discount rate and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL > 3% for the subsequent 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a softening labor market, which erodes consumer and business confidence and typically precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE increases by > 0.2% month-over-month over two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the next 60 days are positive despite repeated soft-labor signals.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in retail sales (PAYEMS) while industrial production (INDPRO) continues to expand suggests sector-specific demand imbalances that weigh on consumer sentiment and corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by > 5% month-over-month while INDPRO increases by > 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline in similar demand imbalance regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in the S&P 500 20-day forward return (not directly observable in the evidence set at decision time) is statistically predicted by the cumulative effect of declining real interest rates (inferred from FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL interaction) over a 12-month horizon, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: Over 100 backtests spanning 5 macro regimes, the 20-day forward return forecast error exceeds 1.5 standard deviations in absolute value more than 30% of the time.
